content.thinking:
Memory climbs steadily from 17:32 with no corresponding traffic increase, and latency follows suit from 17:51 on. With no deploys in 24h, a flat request volume, and no process restart, this points to a classic memory leak driving GC pressure and rising latency as the heap fills up.

The ClientDisconnected errors line up with shoppers timing out on slow responses, further confirming that GC pauses from the leak are causing latency spikes and connection drops. Everything fits the resource-leak model well, so I'm confident in this diagnosis.

hypotheses.summary: Memory usage climbs continuously from 17:31 onward (458MB -> 1.37GB) while request_volume stays flat at 1200/min and the process is never restarted (process_start_time_seconds unchanged throughout). Latency (p50/p95/p99) begins rising in lockstep from ~17:50 onward as the heap approaches its 2GiB limit, and client-facing errors are ClientDisconnected (shoppers timing out while the slowing service holds their requests). No deploy or config change was recorded in the prior 24h, ruling out a bad deploy or config change as the trigger. This is the signature of a resource leak: consumption grows with time/requests-processed rather than with traffic, degrading the process until it is memory- and latency-bound.

supporting_evidence.claim: WARN io-shop: heap at 1045MiB of 2048MiB limit
WARN io-shop: heap at 1315MiB of 2048MiB limit
request_volume constant at 1200 for every minute across the entire span
process_start_time_seconds identical (1790402448.765191) across the whole span, i.e. no restart occurred while memory climbed

hypotheses.summary: If the memory/latency climb is not a leak internal to io-shop, it could instead reflect growing pressure from a dependency it calls during account-page rendering (io-pricing or io-summary-cache, both owned internally by checkout-platform) causing requests to be held open longer, but the logs show no errors or slowness attributed to those calls - only generic ClientDisconnected entries - so this is weakly supported.

supporting_evidence.claim: io-summary-cache: internal, owned by checkout-platform ... Optional by design - the page is correct without it
io-pricing: internal, owned by checkout-platform ... Called while the account page renders
